title: The Anatomy of a Sincere Apology
subtitle: 用准确、真诚的英语承认伤害、承担责任，并修复关系。

items.meaning: 承认；正视（事实、感受或影响）
items.example: A sincere apology begins by acknowledging the harm you caused.
She took responsibility for speaking carelessly.
He offered to make amends by replacing the damaged book.
Try not to become defensive when someone explains why they were hurt.
Saying “It was no big deal” can sound dismissive.

items.meaning: 担当；对自己的行为负责
items.example: Trust is easier to rebuild when an apology shows real accountability.
Consistent actions are necessary to rebuild trust after a broken promise.

sections.label: Reading
sections.title: 英语短文
sections.heading: More Than Saying Sorry
paragraphs: A good apology is not a performance designed to end an uncomfortable conversation. It is a way of showing that you understand another person’s experience. Saying “I’m sorry you feel that way” often fails because it focuses on the listener’s reaction rather than the speaker’s behavior. A sincere apology names the action and acknowledges its impact: “I’m sorry I interrupted you repeatedly. That was disrespectful.”

The next step is accountability. Explanations may provide context, but they should not become excuses. Compare “I was stressed, so I snapped at you” with “I was stressed, but that did not justify snapping at you.” The second sentence accepts responsibility while still explaining what happened. It also avoids becoming defensive or dismissive.

A thoughtful apology may express regret and propose a repair. You might say, “I wish I had listened more carefully. What can I do to make amends?” However, the person who was hurt is not required to forgive immediately. They may need time, and pressuring them can weaken the apology.

Finally, behavior matters more than perfect wording. If you promise to change but repeat the same action, trust will continue to decline. Rebuilding trust requires consistent evidence: listening without interrupting, keeping agreements, and correcting mistakes early. An apology opens the door to repair, but changed behavior is what allows the relationship to move through it.

items.pattern: I wish + subject + had + past participle
items.explanation: 用于表达对过去行为的遗憾。wish 后用过去完成时，表示希望过去发生过不同的情况。
items.example: I wish I had listened before giving advice.

items.explanation: 表示“为……承担责任”。for 后接名词或动名词，不接动词原形。
items.example: I take responsibility for making a decision without consulting you.

items.question: I wish I ______ (not / dismiss) your concerns so quickly.
用 take responsibility for 改写：I admit that I shared the news without permission.
According to the passage, why can an explanation weaken an apology, and how can the speaker prevent that?

sections.label: Check Your Work
sections.title: 答案
items: I take responsibility for sharing the news without permission.

An explanation can weaken an apology when it becomes an excuse that avoids accountability. The speaker can provide context while clearly stating that the circumstances did not justify the harmful behavior.
